newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan protesters land on Japan-held isles -radio.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan protesters land on Japan-held isles -radio.

text.p: As many as four Taiwan protesters defied Japanese coastal patrols on Monday and landed on an East China Sea archipelago to claim the isles back from Japan, Taiwan state radio said.

"Four people have succeeded in landing and raising the Republic of China national flag," the station said, quoting ship-to-shore radio reports from a flotilla of about 50 Taiwan boats seeking to make the landing.

One Taiwan protest boat managed to pierce a tight cordong of up to 30 Japanese patrol boats and get near enough to the islets for four activists to swim ashore, according to radio reports from the islands, roughly equidistant between Taiwan and Japan's southernmost major island of Okinawa.

It was not immediately known whether Japanese coastal patrol personnel had gone ashore to confront the four activists. Japan claims the chain as the Senkakus. Taiwan and China claim them as the Diaoyus.
"The four have put up our Republic of China flag and are walking towards the lighthouse," a state radio reporter said from the protest flotilla.

Activists had vowed to remove Japan's flag and the lighthouse, which was erected in July by a Japanese rightist group to assert Tokyo's sovereignty in a move that sparked angry protests among Chinese in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and China.
